studies.title: Nutritional Adjuvants in Diabetes: Biotin and Chromium Picolinate as Emerging Therapeutic Agents.
studies.abstract:
Introduction

Insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are serious worldwide health issues linked to dyslipidaemia, oxidative stress, impaired glucose metabolism, and persistent inflammation. Although their clinical significance is still unknown, micronutrients like chromium and biotin are thought to affect insulin signalling, glucose homeostasis, and lipid metabolism. The purpose of this review is to compile the preclinical, clinical, and epidemiological data that is currently available regarding the individual and combined effects of chromium and biotin on metabolic outcomes, insulin sensitivity, and glycaemic control.

Methods

Using databases like PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar, a thorough search of narrative literature was carried out. Included were pertinent experimental, clinical, and review studies evaluating the use of chromium and/or biotin supplements in diseases like metabolic syndrome, insulin resistance, and type 2 diabetes. With a focus on study design, dosage, duration, mechanistic pathways, and reported metabolic outcomes, the evidence was qualitatively examined.

Results

Preclinical research repeatedly shows that biotin and chromium improve oxidative stress markers, lipid profiles, insulin sensitivity, and glucose tolerance. Increased GLUT-4 translocation, AMPK activation, insulin signalling pathway modulation (IRS-1/PI3K/Akt), and biotin-dependent enzyme regulation are some of the mechanisms that mediate these effects. Particularly in those with poor glycaemic control or micronutrient deficiencies, clinical trials show modest but significant improvements in fasting blood glucose, HbA1c levels, insulin resistance indices, and lipid parameters. Glycaemic control, dyslipidaemia, oxidative stress, and cardiovascular risk markers all seem to improve with combined supplementation. Additionally, epidemiological data point to a negative correlation between dietary chromium consumption and the risk of T2DM.

Discussion

The results demonstrate the complementary functions of biotin and chromium in controlling the metabolism of fats and carbohydrates. When taken together, they may provide greater metabolic advantages than when taken separately. However, the generalisability of findings is constrained by variations in study design, participant characteristics, supplement formulations, and baseline nutritional status. The necessity of standardized research methods is highlighted by these discrepancies.

Conclusion

In general, chromium and biotin exhibit promise as supplemental treatments for the treatment of insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes, especially in populations with nutritional deficiencies or metabolic disorders. However, more extensive, carefully planned randomized controlled trials are needed to ascertain the best dosage, long-term safety, and clinical effectiveness.

studies.title: Chromium Supplementation Reduces Resting Heart Rate in Patients with Metabolic Syndrome and Impaired Glucose Tolerance.
studies.abstract: Chromium (Cr) is considered as an important mineral, involved in biochemical reactions in human metabolic pathways. Organically bound Cr supplementation has been suggested to improve glycemia especially in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, but there are conflicting reports on efficacy. Effect of Cr is not clear in prediabetes status. Seventy patients with metabolic syndrome and impaired glucose tolerance (IGT), who are observed and treated in the Center of Preventive Cardiology of the University Hospital in Pilsen, were included in the prospective, randomized, double-blind, and placebo-controlled clinical study. Effect of Cr-enriched yeast (200 μg of elementary Cr in the morning and 100 μg in the evening) on glucose, lipid metabolism, fat tissue hormones, oxidative stress, and DNA damage markers was analyzed. There were no significant changes in glucose and lipid parameters, oxidative stress, or other laboratory markers. Only resting heart rate was significantly reduced in patients treated by Cr yeast, reflecting reduced sympathetic activity. This could represent an important cardiovascular risk reduction in patients with high cardiometabolic risk.

studies.title: Influence of chromium-enriched yeast on blood glucose and insulin variables, blood lipids, and markers of oxidative stress in subjects with type 2 diabetes mell
studies.abstract: The aim of this study was to determine the effect of chromium (Cr)- enriched yeast on blood glucose and insulin variables, blood lipids, and blood markers of oxidative stress in persons with type 2 diabetes mellitus (median duration: 3.0 yr). Thirty-six subjects (9 men, 27 women; mean age: 61.3 yr; mean body mass index: 34.33 kg/m2) were supplemented with 400 microg Cr/d as Cr-enriched yeast (n = 19) or placebo (n = 17) for 12 wk in a randomized, double-blind study. The most interesting results were obtained by comparison of the change in the placebo group to the change in the Cr group. The Cr group showed a significantly greater increase in serum Cr compared to the placebo group (p < 0.05). Supplementation with Cr-enriched yeast was associated with a significant decrease in fasting serum glucose compared to placebo (p < 0.01). Blood markers of oxidative stress glutathione peroxidase activity and levels of reduced glutathione were essentially unchanged in the Cr group after 12 wk, but decreased significantly in the placebo group (p < 0.05, p < 0.01, respectively). Serum HbA1c and glycated protein (fructosamine) were essentially unchanged in the Cr group, whereas HbA1c tended to increase in the placebo group (from 6.94% to 7.11%). Fasting serum insulin decreased in both groups, with a greater tendency in the Cr group (-16.5% vs -9.5%). These data suggest that supplementation of well-controlled type 2 diabetics with Cr-enriched yeast is safe and can result in improvements in blood glucose variables and oxidative stress.

studies.title: Antioxidant effects of chromium supplementation with type 2 diabetes mellitus and euglycemic subjects.
studies.abstract: To determine the effects of chromium (Cr) supplementations on oxidative stress of type 2 diabetes and euglycemic (EU) subjects, adult having HbA(1C) values of <6.0% (EU), 6.8-8.5% (mildly hyperglycemic, MH), and >8.5% (severely hyperglycemic, SH) were supplemented for 6 months with 1000 microg/day of Cr (as Cr yeast) or with a placebo. In the beginning, the levels of the plasma Cr in the MH and SH groups were 25-30% lower than those of the EU subjects. The values of thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS) and total antioxidative status (TAS) of the MH and SH groups were significantly higher than those of the EU ones. Following supplementations, the levels of plasma TBARS in the Cr groups of MH and SH groups were significantly decreased (the inverse was found in the EU) and showed no significant changes in the placebo group. The levels of plasma TAS in the Cr groups of EU and MH were significantly decreased (the inverse was found in the SH) and showed no significant changes in the placebo group. No significant difference was found in the antioxidant enzyme (superoxide dismutase, glutathione peroxidase, catalase) activities during supplementations. These data suggest that Cr supplementation was an effective treatment strategy to minimize increased oxidative stress in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients whose HbA(1C) level was >8.5%, and the Cr in EU groups might act as a prooxidant.

studies.title: Effects of co-supplementation of chromium and magnesium on metabolic profiles, inflammation, and oxidative stress in impaired glucose tolerance.
studies.abstract: To evaluate the effects of chromium (Cr) and magnesium (Mg) ions on metabolic profiles, inflammation, and oxidative stress with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) and insulin resistance (IR). 120 individuals with IGT and IR were randomly divided into four groups treated with (1) chromium, (2) magnesium, (3) chromium and magnesium or (4) placebo. studies.title: Effects of dietary supplementation of chromium methionine chelate on growth performance, oxidative stress, hematological indices, and carcass traits of broiler
studies.abstract: This study was conducted to evaluate the dietary effects of chromium methionine (Cr-Meth) chelate on growth performance, oxidative stress parameters, blood biochemistry, and carcass traits of broiler chickens. An experiment was conducted on 34,000 1-day-old straight-run broiler chicks (Indian River; 42.0 ± 0.03) at a commercial farm. The chicks were divided randomly into 3 groups; the first group contained 17,000 birds, which used as a control, whereas the second and third groups consisted of 7000 and 10,000 birds, respectively, with 5 replicates per group. A completely randomized design was used. The birds were fed the experimental diets containing graded levels of Cr-Meth chelate: 0 (control), 50, and 100 g/ton. This compound consisted of chromium (0.4%) chelated with methionine, and it supply the diets with 200 and 400 ppb Cr for the used levels of 50 and 100 g/ton feed, respectively. Growth performance indices (body weight, body weight gain, feed intake, and feed conversion ratio) were measured throughout the experiment. At the end of experiment, 10 birds per treatment were slaughtered, and the carcass yield with relative weight of the internal organs was determined. Also, blood samples were taken and analyzed for glutathione peroxidase activity, malondialdehyde, ALT, AST, total protein, albumin, glucose, urea, creatinine, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. It was found that Cr-Meth improved the body weight, weight gain, feed intake, and feed conversion ratio of broilers. Moreover, it reduced the mortality rate of birds. The chelated chromium can alleviate the oxidative status of birds by increasing the plasma glutathione peroxidase activity and reducing the serum malondialdehyde level. It was observed that the effects of 100 g/ton Cr-Meth chelate on performance indices, mortality rate, and oxidative stress parameters were better than that of 50 g/ton inclusion rate. Supplementation of Cr-Meth increased the total protein level, but reduced the glucose, total cholesterol, and triglyceride concentrations in the blood serum. In addition, it increased the carcass yield and reduced the abdominal fat percentage of the birds' carcass. Therefore, chromium can be included in diets of broilers at a rate of 200 to 400 ppb, and the higher concentration was more effective than the lower one. So, it can be recommended to use Cr-Meth chelate in broiler diets at 100 g/ton to improve the productive performance and reduce the oxidative stress of birds.

studies.title: The effect of chromium intake on oxidative stress parameters: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
studies.abstract: Trivalent chromium is a trace element thought to have a beneficial effect on oxidative stress (OS) parameters and inflammation. This review aimed to investigate the dose-response of chromium and summarize the effects of chromium supplementation on OS parameters in the literature. MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane CENTRAL databases were searched for RCTs published from inception to January 2021 evaluating the effect of chromium supplementation on OS parameters, namely MDA, TBARS, SOD, TAS, CAT, GPx, and GSH. A random-effects model was used to pool data and calculated standard mean difference and 95 % confidence intervals. Quantified heterogeneity among studies was assessed through Cochrane's I Nine studies enrolling 550 participants met the inclusion criteria. The obtained results indicate that chromium supplementation significantly increases TAC (SMD: 0.46; 95 % CI: 0.08, 0.84; I Chromium supplementation may improve OS parameters, however, due to high heterogeneity observed in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution. Large RCTs on various patient groups evaluating the impact of chromium supplementation are needed to allow an adequate generalization of the benefits of chromium on human health.

studies.title: Effects of Chromium-Niacin Supplementation on Production and Metabolic Performance in Transition Dairy Cows.
studies.abstract: The objective of this study was to investigate the effects of chromium-niacin (CrNi) supplementation on production parameters, blood metabolites, antioxidant status and serum metabolite profile in transition dairy cows. A total of 28 multiparous Holstein dairy cows were included in the study. The experimental design included two treatments: a control group and a CrNi group, with each cow in the CrNi group receiving 8 mg chromium and 6 g niacin per day. The results showed that CrNi supplementation improved postpartum dry matter intake (DMI), which was higher in the CrNi group (21.02 vs. 19.74 kg/d; P = 0.09). Milk yield was significantly increased by 1.99 kg/d in the CrNi group (39.55 vs. 37.56 kg/d; P = 0.04). Somatic cell count (SCC) was numerically lower in the CrNi group (217 vs. 414 × 10³ cells/mL; P = 0.08), indicating a possible improvement in udder health. Milk protein, fat, lactose and solids-not-fat percentages and yields were not significantly affected by the treatment. Body condition score (BCS) remained similar between groups. No treatment differences were found in serum calcium, BHB, NEFA, alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), urea, glucose, insulin, bilirubin, total protein, albumin, malondialdehyde (MDA) or total antioxidant capacity (TAC). Serum triglyceride levels were affected by CrNi (P = 0.06), with a significant treatment × time interaction (P < 0.05). Metabolomics analysis revealed that 42 metabolites were significantly altered by CrNi supplementation, with 21 metabolites upregulated, particularly those involved in lipid metabolism and microbial co-metabolism. In particular, DG (i-15:0/8:0/0:0) and Vanillic acid 4-O-sulfate were strongly upregulated, indicating increased lipid mobilization. Conversely, 21 metabolites were downregulated, including L-Threonine and Gabexate, indicating suppression of certain metabolic pathways, including anti-inflammatory processes. These results suggest that CrNi supplementation may contribute to improved production performance and metabolic health in transition dairy cows.

studies.title: Remediating effects of coral fossils on hematobiochemical, histo accumulation and organ histomorphological changes in Chromium intoxicated broilers.
studies.abstract: Chromium is one of the most noxious toxins that causes toxic effects in poultry. Coral fossils contain calcium, magnesium and other minerals and have antibacterial, fungistatic and anti-oxidative action. In our previous study, coral fossils showed protective effects against lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd) toxicities in broilers. Our current study evaluated the effects of coral fossil on blood biochemistry and organ histology in chromium (Cr) exposed broilers. 90-day-old broiler chicks were randomly assigned to three equal groups, each containing 30. Group A acted as control, receiving the standard poultry ration. Group B received a daily dose of chromium at 22 mg/kg body weight; meanwhile, Group C received the same chromium dose combined with 1 g/kg body weight of coral fossils. On day 30, blood was collected for hematological and serum biochemical analysis, while samples (muscle, liver, and kidney) were collected for chromium residues (ICP-MS) and histopathology. Results showed that Cr exposure significantly reduced TEC (P < 0.001), Hb (P < 0.001), and PCV (P < 0.001), whereas coral fossil restored TEC (P < 0.001), improved Hb (P < 0.05), and partially restored PCV (P < 0.01). Serum AST (P < 0.01) and ALT (P < 0.05) increased with chromium but declined after coral fossil supplementation (P < 0.01). Coral fossils also reduced serum creatinine (P < 0.01). In the lipid profile, it decreased cholesterol (P < 0.05), triglycerides (P < 0.01), and LDL (P < 0.05), while raising HDL (P < 0.05). Chromium residues in muscle, liver, and kidney were significantly lowered by coral fossil (P < 0.05). In histopathology, severe changes were found in the liver with hepatocyte swelling and perivascular inflammation, also tubular degeneration was found in the kidney in case of chromium treated broiler which was minimized when coral fossil was added. These findings suggest that coral fossil supplementation mitigates chromium-induced physiological disturbances in broiler chickens.

studies.title: Behavioral, Hematological, Biochemical, Antioxidant, Histopathological and Micronuclear Abnormality in the Erythrocytes of Ctenopharyngodon idella Exposed to Ch
studies.abstract: Chromium is characterized by toxicity to living organisms due to their ability to accumulate in biological tissues and disrupt normal physiological functions. The current study assessed the effect of chromium on the serum biochemistry, hematology, antioxidant enzyme system, and histopathology of the selected freshwater fish (Ctenopharyngodon Idella). For this purpose, Ctenopharyngodon Idella, weighing ∼60-80 g, were divided into four groups at random and subsequently subjected to chromium exposure i.e. control, 0.44 mg L⁻¹, 0.89 mg L⁻¹ and 1.34 mg L⁻¹ from LC<sub>50</sub> (74.35 mgL<sup>- 1</sup>) for 21 days and data was taken after 7, 14, and 21 days. Results showed a significant effect of treatment and duration on fish body weight (p < 0.05). A significant increase in leukocytes and heterophils was observed between the treated groups which showed a significant decrease in red blood cell count, hemoglobin, hematocrit, mean corpuscular hemoglobin, mean corpuscular volume, and lymphocytes. Significant reductions (p < 0.05) were observed in serum biochemical parameters such as total proteins, albumin, and globulin. Conversely, the treated groups exhibited significant increases (p < 0.05) in alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), glucose, and cholesterol compared to the control group. Decreased values of antioxidant enzymes, including superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and peroxidase (POD) in the kidney and gills tissues of fish were recorded. The micronucleus (MN) assay confirmed genotoxicity, revealing elevated frequencies of nuclear abnormalities such as notched, condensed, binucleate, pear-shaped nuclei, and micronuclei. There was a noticeable rise in the frequencies of nuclear irregularities within the erythrocytes. The presence of altered nuclei suggests that chromium chloride might be causing damage to the cells and their genetic material. The histopathological analysis of fish gills and kidneys revealed inflammation and degenerative alterations attributed to exposure to chromium. Within kidney tissues, there was an increase in degenerative changes such as expansion of Bowman's space, necrosis of tubular cells, and deterioration of the glomerulus. Congestion, Lamellar fusion, and Lamellar disorganization were observed in the gill's tissues exposed to chromium. In conclusion, the study indicates that exposure to chromium chloride, even in smaller concentrations, can cause adverse hematological and histopathological changes in Ctenopharyngodon Idella.

studies.title: Protective effect of organic selenium and organic chromium dietary supplementation against aflatoxicosis in mice.
studies.abstract: Aflatoxins are highly toxic mycotoxins linked to serious health issues, including hepatotoxicity, immunosuppression, and oxidative stress. This study investigated the protective effects of chromium-methionine (Cr-Met) and selenium-methionine (Se-Met) supplementation, both alone and in combination, against aflatoxin-induced toxicity in mice. Five dietary treatments were implemented: a control diet (T1), an aflatoxin-contaminated diet containing 2 mg of aflatoxins per kg of diet (T2), and aflatoxin-contaminated diets supplemented with 0.5 mg of Cr-Met per kg (T3), 0.5 mg of Se-Met per kg (T4), or a combination of both (T5). Exposure to aflatoxins significantly (p < 0.05) impaired growth performance, disrupted liver enzyme profiles, suppressed immune function, and compromised antioxidant defense mechanisms. In contrast, dietary supplementation with T3 and T4 markedly (p < 0.05) enhanced growth performance, increased feed intake, and elevated immunoglobulin levels while reducing oxidative stress markers and liver damage. Gene expression analysis indicated that aflatoxin exposure led to the upregulation of inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and the downregulation of catalase (CAT), superoxide dismutase (SOD), and glutathione peroxidase (GPx); supplementation effectively reversed these alterations. Notably, the combined supplementation (T5) demonstrated the most significant protective effects, suggesting the role of chromium and selenium in alleviating aflatoxin-induced toxicity (p < 0.05). These findings underscore the potential of using Cr-Met and Se-Met in combination as effective dietary strategies to mitigate aflatoxin toxicity and enhance antioxidant and immune responses.

studies.title: Chromium picolinate supplementation improves cardiac performance in hypoxic rats.
studies.abstract: Conditions associated with chronic hypoxia increase morbidity and mortality attributable to cardiovascular complications. Myocardial hypoxia is a common feature in several diseases including: stroke, infarction, anaemia, chronic lung diseases, obstructive sleep apnoea and cyanotic congenital heart defects. The present study was planned to investigate the cardiovascular effects of chronic intermittent hypoxia and its association with increased myocardial oxidative stress. In addition, to evaluate the protective effect of chromium supplementation, aiming at achieving an alternative that may enable to devise a therapy for hypoxic patients. Male rats were allocated into three groups: control group (normoxic), untreated hypoxic group (exposed to hypoxia 8 h/day, 5 days/week for 6 weeks) and hypoxic group supplemented with chromium picolinate (90 µg/kg/day by gavage). Rats were subjected to measurement of body weight, haematocrit value, mean arterial blood pressure, heart rate and ECG recording. Cardiac activities of isolated hearts were studied on Langendorff preparation under basal conditions and in response to ischaemia/reperfusion. Thereafter, cardiac weights were determined and cardiac tissue catalase activity as well as malondialdhyde level were assessed. Significant results were obtained upon exposure to hypoxia including; low body weight, increased haematocrit, elevated blood pressure, left ventricular hypertrophy and impaired cardiac activities, basally and in response to ischaemia/reperfusion challenges, associated with increased oxidative stress in cardiac tissue. At the same time, chromium supplementation increased body weight, lowered blood pressure, reduced ventricular hypertrophy and significantly improved the cardiac performance. Chromium supplementation confers protection against hypoxia-induced cardiovascular dysfunction by improvement of the antioxidant capacity.

studies.title: Addition of chromium propionate in dog food: metabolic, immunological, and oxidative effects.
studies.abstract: Chromium is a trace element essential in metabolising carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins and is involved in other biological functions. studies.title: The role of dietary chromium supplementation in relieving heat stress of juvenile blunt snout bream Megalobrama amblycephala.
studies.abstract: The present study assessed the role of dietary chromium (Cr) supplementation in relieving heat stress (HS) of juvenile blunt snout bream Megalobrama amblycephala. The supplemented Cr contents by chromium picolinate (Cr-Pic) was 0 mg/kg (control group), 0.4 mg/kg, 1.6 mg/kg and 12.0 mg/kg, respectively. The fish continued to be fed four diets at suitable temperatures (26 °C) for 2 weeks, and then the temperature was then heated up to 33 °C through thermo-regulated system. The results showed that Cr supplementation had no significant effect on the immune indices and antioxidant indices before HS (P > 0.05). However, Cr supplementation played an important role in relieving HS. After HS, compared with the control group, 1.6 mg/kg and 12.0 mg/kg Cr supplementation groups significantly lowered the plasma glucose level and aspartate transaminase (AST) activity (P < 0.05), and 0.4 mg/kg and 1.6 mg/kg Cr supplementation groups significantly lowered alanine aminotransferase (ALT) activity (P < 0.05). 0.4 mg/kg and 1.6 mg/kg supplementation groups significantly improved hepatic total superoxide dismutase (T-SOD) activity (P < 0.05). Furthermore, 0.4mg/kg-12.0 mg/kg Cr supplementation groups significantly improved the activities of hepatic glutathione peroxidase (GPx) and catalase (CAT) and lowered hepatic malondialdehyde (MDA) level in liver (P < 0.05). The mRNA levels of hepatic copper zinc superoxide dismutase (Cu/Zn-SOD), CAT and GPx were significantly improved in 0.4mg/kg-12.0 mg/kg supplementation Cr groups (P < 0.05), however, there was no significant variation of hepatic manganese superoxide dismutase (Mn-SOD) mRNA levels under different levels of supplementation (P > 0.05). Significantly lower mRNA levels of hepatic pro-inflammatory cytokines observed in 0.4mg/kg-12.0 mg/kg Cr supplementation groups including tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin 1β (IL-1β) and interleukin 8 (IL-8) (P < 0.05), and 0.4mg/kg-12.0 mg/kg Cr supplementation significantly improved the relative expressions of hepatic heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) and heat shock protein 90 (HSP90) (P < 0.05). The present study indicated that dietary Cr supplementation might have no significant effect on immune capacity and antioxidant capacity under normal physiological conditions, whereas it played an important role in relieving HS.

studies.title: Trivalent chromium supplementation ameliorates adjuvant induced rheumatoid arthritis through up-regulation of FOXP3 and decrease in synovial Cathepsin G express
studies.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a known debilitating autoimmune disease. Immune-suppressants that are used for disease treatment have serious side effects, therefore, trivalent chromium (Cr (III)); which has shown evidence of its influences on some inflammatory pathways and cytokines; was used in this study for the first time to be assessed for its therapeutic effect in RA rat model and was compared to prednisolone in a trial to find a treatment with lesser side effects. Adult male albino rats were randomly divided into four groups: normal, untreated RA, prednisolone treated RA (1.25 mg/kg/day) and Cr (III) treated RA groups (80 μg/kg/day), induction of RA was done by subcutaneous complete Freund adjuvant injection. Study duration was 4 weeks throughout which arthritis scoring and weight measurement were pursued. Histopathological examination and immunohistochemical FOXP3 assessment were done for joint biopsies. Serum inflammatory markers (interleukin 17, interleukin 10, CRP) and synovial erosive arthritis marker (Cathepsin G) were measured. HDL and non-HDL cholesterol were estimated as well. Cr (III) treatment showed marked clinical and histopathological improvement, also astonishing anti-inflammatory effects (increase in FOXP3 expression and interleukin 10, with decrease in interleukin 17, CRP and synovial Cathepsin G) to the extent that Cr (III) effects on inflammation abolishment were comparable to that of prednisolone and even better at some aspects. Moreover, Cr (III) was protective from side effects, i.e., weight gain and dyslipidemia that were seen with prednisolone treatment. Cr (III) is promising in treating RA and it lacks some side effects of accustomed immune-modulatory agents including prednisolone. Further experimental studies and clinical trials should be held to see the efficacy of Cr (III) in different doses and to assess its long term side effects when used for rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases treatment.

studies.title: Zinc, selenium and chromium co-supplementation improves insulin resistance by preventing hepatic endoplasmic reticulum stress in diet-induced gestational diabet
studies.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is one of the most common pregnancy complications and results in adverse outcomes for pregnant women and their offspring. Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress is associated with insulin resistance and implicates in the development of GDM. Zinc, selenium and chromium have been shown to maintain glucose homeostasis via multiple mechanisms, but how these trace elements affect the insulin resistance and ER stress in GDM are largely unknown. To address this, a GDM rat model was induced by feeding female Sprague-Dawley rats a high-fat (45%) and sucrose diet, while zinc (10 mg/kg.bw), selenium (20 ug/kg.bw), chromium (20 ug/kg.bw) were daily supplemented alone or in combination from 6 weeks before mating to the end of lactation period. Maternal metabolic parameters, hepatic ER stress and insulin signaling were analyzed. The results showed that zinc, selenium and chromium co-supplementation dramatically alleviated high-fat and sucrose-induced glucose intolerance and oxidative stress during entire experiment period. Hepatic ER stress as well as the unfolded protein response was activated in GDM dams, characterized by the up-regulation of glucose-regulated protein 78, phosphorylated the protein kinase RNA-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase, and the inositol-requiring enzyme 1α. Zinc, selenium and chromium supplementation significantly prevented this activation, by which contributes to the promotion of the phosphorylated protein kinase B related insulin signaling and maintenance of glucose homeostasis. In conclusion, zinc, selenium and chromium supplementation may be a promising way to prevent the development of GDM by alleviating hepatic ER stress.

studies.title: Trivalent Chromium Supplementation Ameliorates Oleic Acid-Induced Hepatic Steatosis in Mice.
studies.abstract: Trivalent chromium [Cr(III)] is recognized as an essential trace element for human health, whereas its effect on hepatic lipid metabolism has not yet been fully understood. This study aimed to investigate the beneficial effects and potential mechanisms of Cr(III) on hepatic steatosis in an oleic acid (OA) induced mice model. Mice were fed with high OA for 12 weeks to induce lipid accumulation, and co-administrated with Cr(III) supplementation. Indexes of liver lipid accumulation, associated lipid genes expression, fatty acids (FAs) profile and inflammatory cytokines were analyzed. The data showed that Cr(III) supplementation could attenuate disease progress of hepatic steatosis and protect liver from high OA. After Cr(III) supplementation, elevated body weight and liver injury in steatosis mice were reversed, excessive lipid accumulation and FAs were also reduced. The up-regulation of cluster of differentiation 36 (CD36) and diacylglycerol acyltransferase 2 (DGAT2) following steatosis induction were inhibited by Cr(III). Cr(III) reduced the content of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and TNF-α, IL-12) and restored the level of anti-inflammatory cytokine (IL-10) to the control values. Our results suggest that Cr(III) supplementation is a novel strategy for alleviating OA-induced hepatic steatosis.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A metal element essential for insulin function and glucose metabolism.
explanation.what_it_is: Chromium is a naturally occurring metal element found in small amounts in foods like grains, meat, and vegetables. Your body uses it to help insulin — the hormone that controls blood sugar — work properly. Chromium supplements are sold as picolinate, polynicotinate, or other bound forms, usually in tablets or capsules. It is not produced by your body, so you obtain it entirely from food or supplements.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Enhances how insulin signals cells to take up glucose and stabilizes blood sugar.
explanation.how_it_works: Chromium works by amplifying the signal that insulin sends to your cells. Insulin is a hormone that tells cells 'take up glucose from the blood.' Chromium appears to strengthen this messaging system — think of it as turning up the volume on insulin's instructions. When insulin signaling works better, cells absorb glucose more efficiently, and blood sugar levels stay more stable. The exact molecular steps are still not fully mapped, but the effect shows up consistently in studies of people with high blood sugar or metabolic problems.
explanation.safety_line: Tolerated in short-term trials; long-term and vulnerable-population data are sparse.
explanation.safety_detail: Randomized controlled trials retrieved span weeks to a few months and generally report no serious adverse events. Most studies excluded people with kidney disease, pregnancy, and adolescents — populations in which chromium safety has not been adequately tested. No adequately powered studies on long-term use (years) or drug interactions were found in the records provided.
safety_bullets: Kidney function: Excluded from nearly all trials; chromium is renally cleared, so safety in kidney disease is unknown.
Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Not tested in retrieved studies; status unknown.
Adolescents: Not studied in the records provided; safety and need in youth are untested.
Drug interactions: No interaction studies retrieved; potential for unknown interactions with diabetes or psychiatric medications.
explanation.chem_meaning: Chromium metal is a solid element (atomic number 24) that must be bound to organic molecules — like picolinate or nicotinate — to be absorbed by the digestive tract. These bound forms are water-soluble and stable enough to survive stomach acid, allowing absorption in the small intestine. Once absorbed, chromium accumulates in tissues and is excreted renally, which is why kidney function matters for safety.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Meta-analyses of chromium supplementation in people with type 2 diabetes, prediabetes, and polycystic ovary syndrome show a pooled reduction in blood glucose of approximately 0.99 mmol/L (95% CI −1.72 to −0.25). Data span 26 human studies and 27 animal studies, with 9 independent meta-analyses published between 2017 and 2025 converging on this effect. Most studies lasted 8 to 24 weeks and included people with metabolic dysfunction (diabetes, PCOS, obesity).
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade reflects consistent findings across multiple independent reviews and adequately powered pooled analyses (>2800 participants verified), but limited to short-term trials in specific populations; longer-term effects and efficacy in healthy people remain untested.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Pooled analyses show a small reduction in total cholesterol or lipid profile (mean difference −0.17 mmol/L, 95% CI −0.27 to −0.07), based on 12 human and 12 animal studies. Human evidence derives from 3 primary trials and 8 meta-analyses published between 2018 and 2025, collectively involving over 8400 verified participants. Effects appear most consistent in people with type 2 diabetes and obesity.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate reflects replicated synthesis across multiple reviews and large pooled participant numbers, but the magnitude of effect is small and human primary-trial data are limited (only 3 standalone RCTs identified); the reduction may be clinically modest.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Pooled analysis of 5 human and 1 animal study shows a mean reduction in body weight or fat of approximately 0.5 kg (95% CI −0.97 to −0.03) compared to control. Human evidence comes from 2 primary randomized trials and 3 meta-analyses published between 1996 and 2019, collectively verified at ~1316 participants. One 2018 systematic review in PCOS patients concluded chromium did not meaningfully affect weight or metabolic variables.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade reflects some pooled signal and replication across reviews, but the effect size is small, heterogeneous (ranges from loss to no change), and based on few primary human trials; weight loss of 0.5 kg is within typical noise of daily fluctuation, so clinical significance is unclear.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Nine human and 11 animal studies examined inflammatory and oxidative stress markers (e.g., C-reactive protein, TNF-alpha, antioxidant capacity). Human trials published 2004–2026 include 5 primary RCTs (e.g., studies in metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes, n=27–100 range per trial) and 3 pooled analyses. Most studies lasted 8–24 weeks and reported reductions in oxidative stress biomarkers or inflammatory markers, though effect sizes varied.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate grade reflects convergence across multiple human trials and animal models, but human evidence is limited (5 primary studies, ~750 verified participants), heterogeneous in outcomes measured, and short-term; whether chromium reduces clinically meaningful inflammation over years is unknown.

explanation.evidence_base: Evidence is primarily human (26–12 studies per outcome) and supported by animal models, dominated by meta-analyses and systematic reviews published 2017–2025 that pool data from RCTs lasting weeks to months. Pooled effect sizes are small to moderate; consistency across independent reviews is strong (9 meta-analyses converge on blood-sugar effects). The evidence base reflects efficacy in people with metabolic disorders (diabetes, PCOS, obesity) but lacks long-term trials, trials in healthy populations, and trials in vulnerable groups (children, renal disease, pregnancy).
explanation.open_questions: The records provided do not include adequately powered trials in adolescents, pregnant women, or people with chronic kidney disease — populations for which safety and efficacy remain unknown. Most trials are 8–24 weeks; whether benefits persist or accumulate over years, or whether a minimum duration is needed, is not addressed by the studies retrieved. Mechanistic studies in humans (e.g., measuring insulin signaling directly) are sparse; animal data suggest plausible pathways, but translation to sustained clinical outcomes in diverse populations awaits longer-term and more inclusive trials.

appraisal.headline: The evidence base relies heavily on meta-analyses of small, heterogeneous primary trials with inconsistent outcome definitions and missing sample sizes in most abstracts, making the precision of pooled estimates uncertain and effect sizes clinically modest.

Undocumented sample sizes mean pooled precision estimates are speculative, and a few large unpublished or unabstracted trials could materially shift results.

concerns.detail: For lipids, the engine explicitly states 'Limited human evidence: 3 primary human studies and 8 pooled analyses retrieved — below the threshold for the top tier.' For weight loss: '2 primary human studies and 3 pooled analyses retrieved — below the threshold for the top tier.' Despite this explicit threshold violation, both are graded 'Moderate', suggesting the grade may not align with the stated adequacy standard. This is a contradiction within the evidence assessment itself.

concerns.issue: Inflammation outcome lacks extractable pooled effect
concerns.detail: The engine notes 'pooled effect: none extractable' for inflammation despite grading it 'Moderate'. With only 5 of 20 studies reporting sample sizes and heterogeneous outcome measures (oxidative stress biomarkers, heart rate, inflammatory markers), no quantitative synthesis is possible. The grade appears to reflect narrative consistency rather than measurable clinical benefit.

concerns.issue: Modest absolute effect sizes relative to measurement error
concerns.detail: Blood sugar shows mean difference -0.99 [-1.72 to -0.25]; lipids show -0.17 [-0.27 to -0.07]; weight loss shows -0.5 [-0.97 to -0.03]. For blood glucose, the 95% CI spans from clinically meaningful to near-zero; the upper bound of the weight loss CI crosses zero. These magnitudes are within plausible measurement error for many assays and are small compared to pharmacological interventions or lifestyle modification.

concerns.issue: Disease-specific population bias and generalizability limits
concerns.detail: Across outcomes, most trials enrolled patients with type 2 diabetes or PCOS (evident from meta-analysis titles: 'Type 2 Diabetes', 'PCOS', 'Metabolic Syndrome'). Blood sugar, lipid, and inflammatory effects may not generalize to healthy populations or other metabolic disorders. The retrieval appears enriched for diabetic cohorts, which narrows the claim's scope relative to a 'Moderate' tier designation for the mineral broadly.

appraisal.mechanism_check: Chromium is hypothesized to enhance insulin signaling via potentiating insulin receptor tyrosine kinase activity. However, the retrieved records show only *clinical* outcomes (blood glucose, lipids, inflammation) and *animal* mechanistic studies; no human studies directly measuring insulin receptor phosphorylation, chromium bioavailability, or tissue accumulation are visible. The leap from biochemical plausibility (enhanced insulin signaling in vitro/in vivo models) to modest reductions in fasting glucose or HbA1c in diabetic patients is large and bridged only by correlational evidence in the abstracts provided.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that (1) the absolute effect sizes are small and CI-bound, easily explained by publication bias favoring positive results in the meta-analyses; (2) the primary human trial count is 2–5 depending on outcome, below conventional adequacy thresholds explicitly stated in the engine's own assessments; (3) most trials are in disease-enriched (diabetic/PCOS) populations where placebo effects and regression-to-the-mean are pronounced; and (4) the 2018 systematic review titled 'Chromium supplementation does not improve weight loss or metabolic and hormonal variables in patient[s]' contradicts the pooled 'Moderate' grade yet appears in the same retrieval. Heterogeneous designs and outcome measures suggest meta-analyses may conflate noise with signal.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: Large (n ≥ 300 per arm), adequately powered RCTs in healthy populations with pre-registered outcomes, standardized chromium dosing/formulation, and blinded assessment of fasting glucose/HbA1c and lipid panels would clarify whether effects persist outside diabetic cohorts and whether they exceed measurement variability. Robust stratified subgroup analysis by baseline metabolic status and chromium form (picolinate vs. brewer's yeast vs. other) would also be critical, given the heterogeneity evident in the current pooled estimates.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un elemento metálico esencial para la función de la insulina y el metabolismo de la glucosa.
explanation_es.what_it_is: El cromo es un elemento metálico que ocurre naturalmente y se encuentra en pequeñas cantidades en alimentos como granos, carnes y verduras. Tu cuerpo lo utiliza para ayudar a que la insulina —la hormona que controla el azúcar en sangre— funcione correctamente. Los suplementos de cromo se venden como picolinato, polinicotinato u otras formas ligadas, generalmente en tabletas o cápsulas. No es producido por tu cuerpo, por lo que lo obtienes completamente de los alimentos o suplementos.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Mejora cómo la insulina señaliza a las células para que absorban glucosa y estabiliza el azúcar en sangre.
explanation_es.how_it_works: El cromo funciona amplificando la señal que la insulina envía a tus células. La insulina es una hormona que le dice a las células 'absorban glucosa de la sangre'. El cromo parece fortalecer este sistema de mensajería —piénsalo como aumentar el volumen de las instrucciones de la insulina—. Cuando la señalización de la insulina funciona mejor, las células absorben glucosa más eficientemente y los niveles de azúcar en sangre se mantienen más estables. Los pasos moleculares exactos aún no están completamente cartografiados, pero el efecto aparece consistentemente en estudios de personas con azúcar en sangre elevada o problemas metabólicos.
explanation_es.safety_line: Tolerado en ensayos a corto plazo; los datos a largo plazo y en poblaciones vulnerables son escasos.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos controlados aleatorios recuperados abarcan semanas a pocos meses y generalmente no reportan eventos adversos graves. La mayoría de los estudios excluyeron a personas con enfermedad renal, embarazo y adolescentes —poblaciones en las que la seguridad del cromo no ha sido adecuadamente probada—. No se encontraron estudios con poder estadístico adecuado sobre el uso a largo plazo (años) o interacciones medicamentosas en los registros proporcionados.
safety_bullets: Función renal: Excluida de casi todos los ensayos; el cromo se elimina por vía renal, por lo que la seguridad en la enfermedad renal es desconocida.
Embarazo y lactancia: No probado en los estudios recuperados; estado desconocido.
Adolescentes: No estudiado en los registros proporcionados; la seguridad y la necesidad en jóvenes no han sido probadas.
Interacciones medicamentosas: Sin estudios de interacción recuperados; potencial para interacciones desconocidas con medicamentos para la diabetes o psiquiátricos.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: El cromo metálico es un elemento sólido (número atómico 24) que debe estar ligado a moléculas orgánicas —como picolinato o nicotinato— para ser absorbido por el tracto digestivo. Estas formas ligadas son solubles en agua y lo suficientemente estables para sobrevivir el ácido estomacal, permitiendo la absorción en el intestino delgado. Una vez absorbido, el cromo se acumula en los tejidos y se excreta por vía renal, razón por la cual la función renal es importante para la seguridad.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Los metanálisis de suplementación de cromo en personas con diabetes tipo 2, prediabetes y síndrome de ovario poliquístico muestran una reducción agrupada de glucosa en sangre de aproximadamente 0,99 mmol/L (IC 95% −1,72 a −0,25). Los datos abarcan 26 estudios humanos y 27 estudios animales, con 9 metanálisis independientes publicados entre 2017 y 2025 convergiendo en este efecto. La mayoría de los estudios duraron 8 a 24 semanas e incluyeron personas con disfunción metabólica (diabetes, PCOS, obesidad).
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación moderada refleja hallazgos consistentes en múltiples revisiones independientes y análisis agrupados con poder estadístico adecuado (>2800 participantes verificados), pero limitado a ensayos a corto plazo en poblaciones específicas; los efectos a largo plazo y la eficacia en personas sanas siguen sin probarse.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Los análisis agrupados muestran una pequeña reducción en el colesterol total o perfil de lípidos (diferencia media −0,17 mmol/L, IC 95% −0,27 a −0,07), basado en 12 estudios humanos y 12 estudios animales. La evidencia humana proviene de 3 ensayos primarios y 8 metanálisis publicados entre 2018 y 2025, que colectivamente involucran a más de 8400 participantes verificados. Los efectos parecen ser más consistentes en personas con diabetes tipo 2 y obesidad.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación moderada refleja síntesis replicada en múltiples revisiones y números grandes de participantes agrupados, pero la magnitud del efecto es pequeña y los datos de ensayos primarios humanos son limitados (solo se identificaron 3 ECA independientes); la reducción puede ser clínicamente modesta.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: El análisis agrupado de 5 estudios humanos y 1 estudio animal muestra una reducción media en peso corporal o grasa de aproximadamente 0,5 kg (IC 95% −0,97 a −0,03) comparado con control. La evidencia humana proviene de 2 ensayos aleatorios primarios y 3 metanálisis publicados entre 1996 y 2019, verificados colectivamente en ~1316 participantes. Una revisión sistemática de 2018 en pacientes con PCOS concluyó que el cromo no afectó significativamente el peso u otras variables metabólicas.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación moderada refleja alguna señal agrupada y replicación entre revisiones, pero el tamaño del efecto es pequeño, heterogéneo (varía de pérdida a sin cambio) y basado en pocos ensayos primarios humanos; una pérdida de peso de 0,5 kg está dentro del ruido típico de las fluctuaciones diarias, por lo que la significancia clínica es incierta.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Nueve estudios humanos y 11 estudios animales examinaron marcadores inflamatorios y de estrés oxidativo (p. ej., proteína C reactiva, TNF-alfa, capacidad antioxidante). Los ensayos humanos publicados 2004–2026 incluyen 5 ECA primarios (p. ej., estudios en síndrome metabólico y diabetes tipo 2, rango n=27–100 por ensayo) y 3 análisis agrupados. La mayoría de los estudios duraron 8–24 semanas e informaron reducciones en biomarcadores de estrés oxidativo o marcadores inflamatorios, aunque los tamaños del efecto variaron.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación moderada refleja convergencia en múltiples ensayos humanos y modelos animales, pero la evidencia humana es limitada (5 estudios primarios, ~750 participantes verificados), heterogénea en los resultados medidos y a corto plazo; si el cromo reduce la inflamación clínicamente significativa durante años sigue siendo desconocido.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia es principalmente humana (26–12 estudios por resultado) y apoyada por modelos animales, dominada por metanálisis y revisiones sistemáticas publicadas 2017–2025 que agrupan datos de ECA que duraron semanas a meses. Los tamaños de efecto agrupados son pequeños a moderados; la consistencia entre revisiones independientes es fuerte (9 metanálisis convergen en efectos de azúcar en sangre). La base de evidencia refleja eficacia en personas con trastornos metabólicos (diabetes, PCOS, obesidad) pero carece de ensayos a largo plazo, ensayos en poblaciones sanas y ensayos en grupos vulnerables (niños, enfermedad renal, embarazo).
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados no incluyen ensayos con poder estadístico adecuado en adolescentes, mujeres embarazadas o personas con enfermedad renal crónica —poblaciones para las cuales la seguridad y la eficacia siguen siendo desconocidas—. La mayoría de los ensayos duran 8–24 semanas; si los beneficios persisten o se acumulan durante años, o si se necesita una duración mínima, no es abordado por los estudios recuperados. Los estudios mecanísticos en humanos (p. ej., medir la señalización de insulina directamente) son escasos; los datos animales sugieren vías plausibles, pero la traslación a resultados clínicos sostenidos en poblaciones diversas awaits ensayos más largos e inclusivos.

appraisal_es.headline: La base de evidencia se apoya en gran medida en metanálisis de ensayos primarios pequeños y heterogéneos con definiciones de resultados inconsistentes y tamaños de muestra faltantes en la mayoría de resúmenes, lo que hace que la precisión de las estimaciones agrupadas sea incierta y los tamaños de efecto clínicamente modestos.

concerns.issue: Los datos de tamaño de muestra faltantes oscurecen el verdadero volumen de evidencia
concerns.detail: Para glucosa en sangre (26 estudios en humanos), solo 16 de 53 estudios totales reportan n; para pérdida de peso, solo 1 de 6 estudios reporta n; para inflamación, solo 5 de 20 estudios reportan n. El motor señala que 'el total verdadero es sustancialmente mayor' pero esto no puede verificarse a partir de los registros. Los tamaños de muestra no documentados significan que las estimaciones de precisión agrupada son especulativas, y algunos pocos ensayos grandes no publicados o sin resumen podrían cambiar materialmente los resultados.

concerns.issue: El umbral de evidencia para colesterol y pérdida de peso no cumple con la clasificación 'Moderada'
concerns.detail: Para lípidos, el motor explícitamente declara 'Evidencia humana limitada: 3 estudios primarios en humanos y 8 análisis agrupados recuperados — por debajo del umbral para el nivel superior.' Para pérdida de peso: '2 estudios primarios en humanos y 3 análisis agrupados recuperados — por debajo del umbral para el nivel superior.' A pesar de esta violación explícita del umbral, ambos se califican como 'Moderada', lo que sugiere que la calificación podría no alinearse con el estándar de adecuación establecido. Esta es una contradicción dentro de la propia evaluación de evidencia.

concerns.issue: El resultado de inflamación carece de efecto agrupado extraíble
concerns.detail: El motor señala 'efecto agrupado: ninguno extraíble' para inflamación a pesar de calificarlo como 'Moderada'. Con solo 5 de 20 estudios reportando tamaños de muestra y medidas de resultado heterogéneas (biomarcadores de estrés oxidativo, frecuencia cardíaca, marcadores inflamatorios), no es posible síntesis cuantitativa. La calificación parece reflejar consistencia narrativa más que beneficio clínico medible.

concerns.issue: Tamaños de efecto absoluto modestos en relación con el error de medición
concerns.detail: La glucosa en sangre muestra diferencia media -0.99 [-1.72 a -0.25]; los lípidos muestran -0.17 [-0.27 a -0.07]; la pérdida de peso muestra -0.5 [-0.97 a -0.03]. Para glucosa en sangre, el IC del 95% abarca desde clínicamente significativo hasta casi cero; el límite superior del IC de pérdida de peso cruza cero. Estas magnitudes están dentro del error de medición plausible para muchos ensayos y son pequeñas comparadas con intervenciones farmacológicas o modificación del estilo de vida.

concerns.issue: Sesgo específico de la población y limitaciones de generalización
concerns.detail: En todos los resultados, la mayoría de ensayos reclutaron pacientes con diabetes tipo 2 o PCOS (evidente en títulos de metanálisis: 'Tipo 2 Diabetes', 'PCOS', 'Síndrome Metabólico'). Los efectos en glucosa en sangre, lípidos e inflamación podrían no generalizarse a poblaciones sanas u otros trastornos metabólicos. La recuperación parece enriquecida para cohortes diabéticas, lo que estrecha el alcance de la afirmación en relación con una designación de nivel 'Moderada' para el mineral en general.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Se hipotetiza que el cromo mejora la señalización de insulina potenciando la actividad de la tirosina quinasa del receptor de insulina. Sin embargo, los registros recuperados muestran solo resultados *clínicos* (glucosa en sangre, lípidos, inflamación) y estudios mecanísticos *animales*; no hay estudios en humanos que midan directamente la fosforilación del receptor de insulina, biodisponibilidad del cromo o acumulación tisular visibles. El salto desde la plausibilidad bioquímica (señalización de insulina mejorada en modelos in vitro/in vivo) a reducciones modestas en glucosa en ayunas o HbA1c en pacientes diabéticos es grande y se cubre solo con evidencia correlacional en los resúmenes proporcionados.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico señalaría que (1) los tamaños de efecto absoluto son pequeños y están limitados por IC, fácilmente explicables por sesgo de publicación que favorece resultados positivos en los metanálisis; (2) el recuento de ensayos primarios en humanos es de 2–5 dependiendo del resultado, por debajo de los umbrales de adecuación convencionales explícitamente establecidos en las propias evaluaciones del motor; (3) la mayoría de ensayos están en poblaciones enriquecidas con enfermedad (diabéticos/PCOS) donde los efectos placebo y la regresión a la media son pronunciados; y (4) la revisión sistemática de 2018 titulada 'Chromium supplementation does not improve weight loss or metabolic and hormonal variables in patient[s]' contradice la calificación agrupada 'Moderada' sin embargo aparece en la misma recuperación. Los diseños heterogéneos y las medidas de resultado sugieren que los metanálisis pueden confundir ruido con señal.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Ensayos clínicos aleatorizados grandes (n ≥ 300 por rama), adecuadamente potenciados, en poblaciones sanas con resultados preregistrados, dosificación/formulación de cromo estandarizada y evaluación ciega de glucosa en ayunas/HbA1c y paneles de lípidos aclararían si los efectos persisten fuera de cohortes diabéticas y si exceden la variabilidad de medición. El análisis de subgrupo estratificado robusto por estado metabólico basal y forma de cromo (picolinato vs. levadura de cerveza vs. otro) también sería crítico, dada la heterogeneidad evidente en las estimaciones agrupadas actuales.
